title: Use --generate-notes for the release command in RELEASING.md
author: claude
head: df6b68badfcb0d6217199df59a92c7027ed89bf7
body:
Step 5 of `RELEASING.md` created the GitHub release with `--notes "See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for details."`, but the repository has no `CHANGELOG.md`, so the release notes would point at a dead link. The Quick Release one-liner further down already uses `--generate-notes`; this makes the step-by-step command do the same so the two are consistent.

Docs-only change, no code touched.

**Checks run locally**
- `npm run format:check` — passes
- `grep -rn CHANGELOG` — no remaining references

adjudication.reason: the check fails the same way on the base and the head, so it did not discriminate between them

check.contents:
#!/bin/bash
# Check that RELEASING.md uses --generate-notes and has no CHANGELOG references

FAIL=0

# Check 1: No references to CHANGELOG should remain
if grep -qi 'CHANGELOG' RELEASING.md; then
  echo "FAIL: RELEASING.md still contains references to CHANGELOG"
  grep -n 'CHANGELOG' RELEASING.md
  FAIL=1
else
  echo "PASS: No CHANGELOG references found"
fi

# Check 2: --generate-notes must be used in the release command (step 5)
if ! grep -q '\-\-generate-notes' RELEASING.md; then
  echo "FAIL: RELEASING.md does not use --generate-notes for releases"
  FAIL=1
else
  echo "PASS: --generate-notes is used in release command"
fi

# Check 3: The Quick Release script should also use --generate-notes (consistency)
if ! grep -A5 'Quick Release' RELEASING.md | grep -q '\-\-generate-notes'; then
  echo "FAIL: Quick Release script does not use --generate-notes"
  FAIL=1
else
  echo "PASS: Quick Release script uses --generate-notes"
fi

if [ $FAIL -ne 0 ]; then
  exit 1
fi

echo "All checks passed"
exit 0
